Belgian Steel Sector Faces Acute Credit Squeeze as Prices Plunge

Belgium’s steel industry is reeling from a severe credit freeze, triggered by a dramatic collapse in global steel prices over recent weeks. The crisis has left several domestic steelmakers struggling to secure working capital, with some forced to suspend operations at key production sites.

The country’s largest producer, BelSteel, announced on Thursday that it had halted two blast furnaces at its Liège facility after lenders refused to extend short-term credit lines. “The sudden tightening in credit markets has left us with no option but to pause production,” said interim CEO Luc Van der Meer. “Our priority is to stabilize finances and minimize the impact on our workforce.”

According to the Belgian Steel Federation, at least four major plants across Wallonia and Flanders have reduced output or temporarily shut down since the start of the month. “This is the most acute liquidity crisis the sector has faced in over a decade,” said federation president Anne-Marie Declercq. “Without urgent intervention, there is a real risk of long-term damage to Belgium’s industrial base.”

Industry unions estimate that over 2,500 steelworkers are now on partial unemployment schemes, with many more facing reduced hours or temporary layoffs. “Families are anxious and frustrated,” said Marc Dubois, spokesperson for the United Steelworkers Belgium. “Our members are worried about the security of their jobs and the future of the steel industry in this country.”

Analysts warn that, with steel prices down 30% since March and banks increasingly reluctant to extend credit, Belgian steelmakers could face further plant closures and job losses in the coming weeks. Negotiations between company executives, unions, and government officials are ongoing, but no resolution has yet been reached.
